card.name: Unix help and file-listing instructions
card.fires_on: Words inside how-to text about Unix or Linux commands and documentation, such as help, ls, or 'see if' and 'check out what' before a thing to look up or list. It also fires on a few unrelated words in instruction-like sentences.

modes.label: Command words
modes.description: Command names or the word help in computer instructions for viewing or listing things.
modes.example: send E-mail to email@example.com with the word "<<help>>" in the body of the message.

modes.label: Look-up phrasing
modes.description: Small words in sentences telling the reader to check, see or find something on a system.
modes.example: See<< if>> your system has some CD drive: d

modes.label: Stray instruction words
modes.description: Pronouns or linking words in sentences about handling or finding documentation.
modes.example: The /usr/share/doc/ localisation is the place where<< you>> find the documentation in formats other than man

card.writes: It nudges toward words about availability, checking and overviews, such as 'available', 'availability' and 'overview'.
